page: Amazon Web Services c5.18xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a dedicated 36-core Intel Xeon 8223CL processor operating at 3.4 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, presenting 72 vCPUs via two threads per core. The instance provides 144.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, establishing a fixed 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Local storage is not bundled, requiring external network-attached volumes for persistent data, and network throughput is provisioned at a baseline rate of 25 Gbps without dedicated GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute performance, reflected by a stress-ng multi-core result of 66687.24 and a PassMark CPU score of 49988.17. High-throughput vector processing is supported by AVX-512 extensions, evidenced by an extended instructions score of 67017.72. Memory throughput remains robust under load, achieving 208.99 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 92.77 GB/sec on writes. Single-threaded metrics, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1189.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1425.19, align with standard mid-range profiles.

Resource efficiency is centered on multi-threaded compute density, optimizing operational value for scale-out parallel tasks that saturate CPU cores rather than memory footprints. However, the lack of hardware accelerators results in weak text generation throughput for large language models, and storage-intensive tasks require consideration of network storage latency due to the absence of local disks. The instance is suited for batch processing, scientific simulations, Clang compilation jobs, video encoding, and high-concurrency database operations.
description: Amazon Web Services c5.18xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 8223CL processor running at 3.4 GHz. Delivering 72 vCPUs across 36 physical x86_64 cores with simultaneous multithreading, it provides 144.0 GB of DDR4 memory at a consistent 2.0 GB per vCPU allocation. The configuration includes 25 Gbps baseline network throughput, zero hardware GPUs, and no bundled local instance storage. Benchmark tests reflect strong multi-core processing with a stress-ng multi-core score of 66687.24 and robust memory bandwidth of 208.99 GB/sec on uncached reads, while single-core metrics sit at intermediate tiering. Given the compute-heavy resource ratio, the instance is engineered for highly parallel workloads, distributed batch computing, software compilation pipelines, and multi-threaded data processing systems.
